proposal.hypothesis: Li3PO4 is a wide-gap (about 5 eV) electronic insulator with a phosphate framework that is chemically compatible with both LiCoO2 and the sulfide electrolyte. It is a well-known protective coating that can limit Co-S interdiffusion and oxidative decomposition at 4.0 V, so it is a strong first candidate for the stability penalty.

LiF is a wide-gap insulator with very high oxidative stability at 4.0 V and no P, S, or O anion that can exchange with the sulfide electrolyte. Li3PO4 failed because its P-O framework reacted with Li6PS5Cl to form P2O5, SO2 and SCl4, so a fluoride with only Li and F should avoid that contact reaction and lower the penalty.
